overview: The file consists chiefly of cross-reference sheets directing researchers to documents filed elsewhere concerning the wartime ownership, registry, charter, sale, and proposed exchange of merchant vessels connected with Japan. Its subjects include the contemplated sale of the Sun Oil Company tanker J. N. Pew to Mitsui through nominal Thai purchasers, restrictions on transferring Panamanian vessels to Japanese registry, possible U.S. chartering of Japanese merchant ships, the movements of foreign vessels reported from Montevideo, and a proposal to exchange Pacific territories for Japanese ships. Together, the documents illuminate official concern over disguised transactions, flag transfers, shipping shortages, and the possible diplomatic use of merchant shipping in U.S.–Japanese relations during 1940–1941.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on proposed sale of tanker J. N. Pew to Mitsui
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a British Embassy memorandum reporting that the Sun Oil Company was considering selling the tanker J. N. Pew to Mitsui through nominal purchasers in Thailand.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference points to a memorandum in file 195.2/3790. According to the subject note, the British Embassy reported a contemplated Sun Oil Company sale of the tanker J. N. Pew to Mitsui, with Thai purchasers serving as a cloak for the Japanese acquisition.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on transferring Panamanian vessels to Japanese registry
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a telegram concerning Panamanian restrictions on cancelling vessel registrations for transfer to Japanese registry.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office reported that on March 27 the Ministry of Finance issued a telegraphic circular to Panamanian consular officers. The circular instructed them not to cancel certificates of Panamanian registry without prior authorization, a measure relevant to contemplated transfers of vessels to Japanese registry. The referenced original is telegram no. 74 of April 9, 1941, filed under 819.852/25.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on U.S. chartering of Japanese merchant vessels
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a memorandum suggesting that the United States charter Japanese merchant vessels as a conciliatory step in relations with Japan.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference records a proposal that the United States charter Japanese merchant ships. The measure was presented as one of several steps that could preserve American principles while demonstrating that relations between the United States and Japan were still being maintained. The original memorandum is identified as part of file 711.94/2406-8/11.

subfiles.title: Correction slip for Montevideo telegram no. 318
subfiles.about: The slip records corrections associated with telegram no. 318 from Montevideo concerning movements of foreign boats.
subfiles.summary: This correction record identifies the origin as Montevideo, the number as 318, and the transmission time as December 24, 1940, at 6 p.m. Its subject is the movement of foreign boats, and it notes a correction concerning departure on December 24. The duplicated instruction to strike out and insert serial number 318 may reflect a typographical or OCR problem in the form.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on exchanging Pacific territories for Japanese ships
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a memorandum submitting a proposal to exchange unspecified Pacific territories for Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference points to a State Department memorandum proposing an exchange of certain Pacific territories for Japanese vessels. The abbreviated routing directs the document to Hamilton in Far Eastern Affairs. The underlying memorandum is filed under 711.94/2540-17/35.

interest: The file is useful because it brings together several ways in which merchant shipping became entangled with diplomacy, sanctions-era commercial maneuvering, flag registration, and strategic bargaining immediately before the Pacific War. Particularly revealing are the allegation that Thai buyers would conceal a sale to Mitsui and the striking proposal to exchange Pacific territories for Japanese ships. Because most pages are cross-references rather than the underlying papers, the bundle also documents the State Department’s filing practices and identifies related decimal-file materials that a historian could pursue.
